Restrict a BRIER fit or selection to some of its eta values

subsetEta.Rd

Returns the same kind of object, restricted to the requested rows of the eta grid, so predict(), coef() and the plots work on it unchanged. The typical use is the no-transfer comparison: subsetEta(sel, eta = 0) is the target-only model of the same fit, with its own best lambda.

Usage

subsetEta(object, eta = NULL, which.eta = NULL, tol = 0.01)

Arguments

object

An object of class "BRIER" (a fit, or a tuned "BRIER.selection" / "BRIER.cv" object).

eta

Eta values to keep: a numeric vector when there is one external model (or one stacked predictor), or a matrix with one column per external model, one row per eta combination.

which.eta

Alternatively, integer row indices into object$eta.grid. Give eta or which.eta, not both.

tol

Relative tolerance for matching eta to the fitted grid. Default 0.01.

Value

An object of the same class as object, with res, eta.grid, eta.list and (if tuned) eta.lambda, eta.min, eta.min.index, lambda.min, lambda.min.index restricted and re-indexed, and eta.subset recording the rows of the original grid that were kept.

Details

  • On a tuned object (from BRIERi.selection, BRIERs.selection, BRIERfull.selection, BRIERi.cv or a *.bopt function), the result is re-selected WITHIN the requested etas: eta.min is the best of them by the original criterion, and lambda.min is that eta's own best lambda. With a single eta, the result is pinned to it.

  • On an untuned fit, the result is the fit restricted to those etas; run a selection function on it as usual.

Only fitted etas can be returned. Values given in eta are matched to the nearest fitted row and accepted when the relative difference |a - b| / max(|a|, |b|) is within tol for every component; a value with no fitted row that close is an error listing the fitted grid (refit with it in eta.list to use it).

See also

predict.BRIER, coef.BRIER, BRIERi.selection, BRIERs.selection

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit <- BRIERi(X, y, family = "gaussian", beta.external = beta.external)
sel <- BRIERi.selection(fit, criteria = "gaussian.mspe", X.val = X.val, y.val = y.val)

# target-only (no transfer) model of the same fit, with its own best lambda
target.only <- subsetEta(sel, eta = 0)
evalMetric(predict(target.only, X.test), y.test, "gaussian.rsq")

# the best model with eta restricted to (0, 1]
small <- subsetEta(sel, eta = sel$eta.grid[sel$eta.grid[, 1] <= 1, 1])
} # }
